'''Cindy Golding''' (born 1952) is an American politician, entrepreneur, farmer and former chemist who has represented the [[Iowa's 83rd House of Representatives district|83rd district]] of the [[Iowa House of Representatives]] since January 2023, which consists of much of rural [[Linn County, Iowa|Linn County]]. She is a member of the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]].<ref name="Legislature">{{cite web |title=State Representative - All Years |url=https://www.legis.iowa.gov/legislators/legislator/legislatorAllYears?personID=33990 |website=Iowa Legislature |access-date=June 2, 2024}}</ref>

==Early life==
Golding was born in 1952 in [[Chicago]], and was raised in rural northern [[Illinois]]. She went to [[Northern Illinois University]] before attending [[Elmhurst University]], where she majored in biochemistry.<ref name=Legislature/>

==Political career==
Golding ran for the [[Iowa's 18th Senate district|18th district]] of the [[Iowa Senate]] in a special election in 2011 to fill a vacancy left by [[Swati Dandekar]]'s resignation, but lost to Democrat [[Liz Mathis]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lynch |first1=James Q. |title=Golding wins Iowa Senate nomination |url=https://www.thegazette.com/news/golding-wins-iowa-senate-nomination/ |website=The Gazette |access-date=June 2, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Cindy Golding still considering Iowa Senate district 48 bid |url=https://www.bleedingheartland.com/2011/11/14/cindy-golding-still-considering-iowa-senate-district-48-bid/ |website=Bleeding Heartland |access-date=June 2, 2024 |language=en |date=14 November 2011}}</ref>

Golding announced her candidacy for the 83rd district of the Iowa House of Representatives shortly after decennial redistricting took place in 2021.<ref name="Gazette">{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Vanessa |title=Family-focused candidates vie for Iowa House 83 |url=https://www.thegazette.com/campaigns-elections/family-focused-candidates-vie-for-iowa-house-83/ |website=The Gazette |access-date=June 2, 2024}}</ref> She won the Republican primaries unopposed on June 7, 2022, and defeated Democrat Kris Nall in the general election on November 8 by over 2,800 votes.<ref name="Ballotpedia">{{cite web |title=Cindy Golding |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Cindy_Golding |website=Ballotpedia |access-date=June 2, 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

Golding endorsed [[Donald Trump]] for president in 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=Trump announces Eastern Iowa endorsements ahead of Davenport event |url=https://theiowastandard.com/trump-announces-eastern-iowa-endorsements-ahead-of-davenport-event/ |website=The Iowa Standard |access-date=June 2, 2024 |date=13 March 2023}}</ref>

In 2024, Golding filed to run for reelection.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Barton |first1=Tom |title=Challengers file to run for Iowa House and Senate seats |url=https://www.thegazette.com/campaigns-elections/challengers-file-to-run-for-iowa-house-and-senate-seats/ |website=The Gazette |access-date=June 2, 2024}}</ref> She won the Republican primaries unopposed on June 4, 2024,<ref name="Ballotpedia" /> and defeated Democrat Kent McNally in the general election on November 5, 2024, receiving 11,321 votes (58.72%) to McNally's 7,947 (41.21%).<ref>{{cite web |date=2025-03-25 |title=Official Results: November 5, 2024 General Election, County of Linn, State of Iowa |url=https://www.linncountyiowa.gov/DocumentCenter/View/25574/11052024-General-Election-Official-Election-Summary-with-Write-ins-PDF |access-date=2025-02-19 |publisher=Linn County, Iowa}}</ref>

Golding currently serves on the Labor and Workforce, Veterans Affairs, State Government, and Local Government committees, the lattermost of which she is vice chair.<ref>{{cite web |title=State Representative - Bills & Committees |url=https://www.legis.iowa.gov/legislators/legislator?ga=90&personID=33990 |website=Iowa Legislature |access-date=June 2, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Golding has a husband, Joe, six adult children, and 21 grandchildren. She resides in rural Linn County. She is the co-founder of Advancement Resources, a training services and research company, and also owns several farms. She worked as an [[analytical chemist]] prior to her business ventures.<ref name=Legislature/><ref name=Gazette/>

Golding has been active in numerous organizations. She is the former chair of the Linn County Republican Party Central Committee and Heartland Youth for Christ, former second vice president of the Iowa Federation of Republican Women, and is a former board member of the [[National Federation of Independent Business]], Five Seasons Republican Women, Linn County [[Farm Bureau]], and Hawkeye Area Community Action Program. She has also worked as an [[National FFA Organization|FFA]] judge, cheerleading coach, [[Academic Decathlon]] coach and judge, [[United States National Chemistry Olympiad|Chemistry Olympiad]] proctor, [[Mathcounts]] coach, church youth leader, and [[Boy Scouts of America|Boy Scout]] and [[Girl Scouts of the USA|Girl Scout]] leader.<ref name=Legislature/>
